newsitem.title: USA: Florida Progress unit reaches union pact.
newsitem.headline: Florida Progress unit reaches union pact.

text.p: Florida Power Corp said it has reached a three-year contract agreement with the International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers union, averting a strike by more than half its workforce.

A spokesman for the utility, the largest subsidiary of Florida Progress Corp, said the agreement was reached Wednesday evening. It would cover 2,050 of the utility's 4,600 employees. A ratification vote is expected May 19.

The company spokesman said the agreement includes a 1.5 percent base pay increase in each year of the three-year agreement, for a 4.5 percent pay increase overall, as well as a 3.5 percent one-time "transition payment" to make up for the workers not having had a pay increase since December 1995.
The previous contract expired in December 1996. Contract talks, which began in September, had broken off in mid-April, but had resumed on Monday.

The contract agreement also would include union members in a company bonus program that previously had been available only to non-union employees and make changes in medical and retirement benefits, Dean said.
Union officials were not immediately available to comment.
Florida Power is the largest subsidiary of Florida Progress, with about 4,600 of the parent company's 7,300 employees.
